THIS IS A GENUINE TWO-WAY BRANCH AND I HAVE MODELLED ONLY THE SPINE. The walkthrough is two bullets long; the rest of the mission lives in four sibling sections that pair up into two whole different routes. Go to San d'Oria first ('Bastok to San d'Oria' then 'San d'Oria to Windurst') and you fight Warchief Vatgit in the Ghelsba Outpost, get the [KI] Dark key from Kupipi, and clear the Black Dragon at Balga's Dais. Go to Windurst first ('Bastok to Windurst' then 'Windurst to San d'Oria') and you instead get the [KI] Sword offering and [KI] Dull sword, kill Eyy Mon the Ironbreaker for an Aspir Knife to trade to Uu Zhoumo, and clear the Dread Dragon at Horlais Peak for the [KI] Kindred crest and [KI] Kindred report. The two routes share almost no content, so there is no merged path a player follows and inventing one would be a marker sending somebody to the wrong BCNM.

What IS common to both orders: Naji at the start with the [KI] Letter to the consuls, Helaku in the Consulate of Bastok in Northern San d'Oria, Melek in the Consulate of Bastok in Port Windurst, and Naji again at the end. Helaku and Melek share a group because the order between them is the player's choice -- that is exactly what a group means -- and they draw together. Every branch-only key item is left out of `evidence` on purpose: each is true on only one of the two routes, so any of them would read false for half the players.

Step source_bullets for rungs 2-4 are numbered within the After sections they came from, which restart at [1]; the notes say which section each is.

steps.note: outside the President's Office, HP #1. He escorts you in to President Karst; the bottom option 'No questions.' skips the interview. The key item arrives at the end of it, which is why both bullets are one rung.

His arm continues to Halver in Chateau d'Oraguille (I-9) and then to a fight, but WHICH fight depends on the order you chose, so it is not modelled.

The judgement call here is that the [KI] Delkfutt key is NOT used as evidence anywhere, and it is the only key item the middle of the mission produces. The page's own Notes say outright that you do not have to be on this mission to get a Delkfutt Key from Porphyrion, and the key item persists; a player who climbed the tower on another character's errand, or who did San d'Oria's or Windurst's 3-3, walks in already holding it. Using it would jump the ladder straight to the embassy door in Ru'Lude Gardens while the Basement cutscene is still undone -- a marker sending somebody to the wrong city. So this mission carries evidence only at rung 1, and that is the honest reading.

The climb is not modelled either. Three of the four After sections ('Obtaining Delkfutt Key Short Way', 'Obtaining Delkfutt Key', 'Navigation') are two alternative routes up thirteen floors of Delkfutt's Tower to Porphyrion; they are ways to satisfy rung 3's item requirement, not rungs. What I did take from 'Finishing the Mission' is the door grid, because the walkthrough's own '(K/L-9)' is useless without the warning that Windurst's door is at (L-7)/(M-7) and San d'Oria's at (L-8)/(M-8) and the wrong one gives no cutscene.

Both Cermet Door rungs carry the Delkfutt Key item in `items` and the key item variant in `items_alt`, which is exactly the 'items OR any one of items_alt' the field is for. Medium, for the two unmodelled routes and the missing middle evidence.

I DISAGREE WITH chronicle_snpc HERE AND THE MARKER MOVES. Chronicle's giver is the string "bastokan embassy in ru'lude gardens", which is the header's Start field verbatim -- a place, not an entity, and nothing the by_npc index can have a row for. The walkthrough's own bullet 1 says to speak with GOGGEHN and then click the innermost Door: Bastokan Emb., both in Ru'Lude Gardens (H-10), and Goggehn is also who you return to at bullet 7. So start.npc is Goggehn: a real NPC standing at the place chronicle was pointing at, which turns a marker that could not be drawn into one that can. Flagged start_disagrees_with_header.

The walkthrough proper is a seven-bullet summary and the mission is in the six After sections. The three magicites are a genuine unordered set, so they share a group and draw together -- but the evidence for all three sits on the LAST group member only. That is deliberate and it is the batch4 monuments reasoning: core/steps.lua takes a high-water mark, so one magicite key item per arm would advance the whole ladder past the other two arms the instant a player finished whichever they chose first, leaving the mark on the Audience Chamber with two magicites missing. An AND-list on the last rung advances only when all three are held.

The [KI] Silver bell carries NO evidence, because the page says in so many words that if you did this mission for another nation you already hold it and must still take Aldo's cutscene. Holding it proves nothing about this run. The same latent risk applies in principle to the Archducal audience permit and the Letter to Aldo, but the page raises it only for the bell, and those two are handed over at their own rungs, so they are kept.

The two Sattal-Mansal trades are two rungs because the page insists they must be separate trades or the second key item never arrives; they are consecutive on the same NPC and so draw one marker. Both key items sit on the SECOND of the two, because the page never says which of the Quadav Charm and the Quadav Augury Shell yields the Coruscant rosary and which the Black matinee necklace, and guessing a pairing would be an assertion the page does not support.

[KI] Message to Jeuno (Bastok), granted by the final Goggehn cutscene, does not resolve against res/key_items.lua and is in any case a completion reward, so it is not used. Medium overall: the ordering inside each magicite arm, the Delkfutt-style route notes, and the Tenshodo membership prerequisite are all real content that no ladder position can express.
